pages.title: Vegetables
pages.text: Vegetables are hearty, grounding foods. $(#e05252)Penalty:$() reduced movement speed when depleted. $(#52c252)Bonus:$() improved hunger saturation when maintained. Carrots, potatoes, and beetroot all qualify.

pages.title: Vanilla Vegetable Sources
pages.text:
$(bold)Carrot$() — found in village farms or zombie drops; very easy to obtain early.
$(bold)Potato$() — also found in villages; bake for higher nutrition value.
$(bold)Baked Potato$() — cook any potato for a significant nutrition boost.
$(bold)Beetroot$() — grown from seeds; lower yield than carrots but still reliable.

pages.title: Golden Carrot
pages.text:
$(bold)Golden Carrot$() is the single highest-nutrition vanilla vegetable. It fills the bar noticeably more than a plain carrot and also provides excellent hunger saturation.

If you have a gold surplus, a small stock of golden carrots makes a great emergency top-up for the Vegetables group.

pages.title: Farming Tips
pages.text:
Carrots and potatoes are the most efficient vanilla vegetables to farm — they replant themselves and grow quickly with irrigation.

A mixed row of carrots, potatoes, and beetroot covers three distinct vegetable families. Plant them side by side in alternating rows to make rotating your diet effortless.

pages.title: Vegetables — Farm & Charm
pages.text: Farm & Charm adds tomatoes, onions, peppers, and more. These introduce new vegetable families and significantly expand rotation options. See the $(bold)Compat Mods$() chapter for the full Farm & Charm food list.

pages.title: Vegetables — Vanilla
pages.text:
Without Farm & Charm, beetroot is your best secondary vegetable alongside carrots and potatoes. A small mixed crop farm covers this group reliably from early game onward.

Beetroot soup counts as Vegetables and provides more nutrition per craft than raw beetroot alone.

pages.title: Rotation Strategy
pages.text:
The main vanilla vegetable families are Carrot, Potato, and Beetroot. Rotating through all three maximizes your nutrition gain compared to eating only one type.

Noting that $(bold)baked potato$() and $(bold)raw potato$() share a family — cooking improves nutrition value but does not count as variety. Use both baked and raw in a pinch, but branch out to carrots and beetroot for best results.
